works.author: alondra-nelson
works.title: Three Fallacies: Alondra Nelson's Remarks at Élysée Palace on the Occasion of the AI Action Summit
works.note: Full text of her own prepared remarks, bylined to Nelson (editor's intro by Justin Hendrix), ~650 words. Rejects three 'fallacies': that AI's purpose is efficiency/scale (vs. people), that safety/rights trade off against innovation (regulation-does-more-harm: disagrees), and that public benefit is inevitable (direction-of-technology-is-chosen: agrees; market-tech-serves-humans: not by markets alone). Focus on present harms (discrimination, security, cohesion); does not discuss extinction risk.

works.author: alondra-nelson
works.title: Regulating AI in the Evolving Transatlantic Landscape
works.channel: Center for American Progress (chapter in 'Trade, Trust, and Transition' report)
works.note: Chapter bylined to Nelson alone within a CAP report, ~1,850 words, public. Argues for targeted enforceable 'red lines' (bans on public real-time biometric ID, automated firing, algorithmic insurance denials) rather than a comprehensive law; says good regulation spurs innovation; criticises Trump/Vance deregulation and Musk's combined roles. Covers binding-rules-for-frontier-ai, regulation-does-more-harm, deployment-harms-over-superintelligence.

works.author: alondra-nelson
works.title: Remarks of Dr. Alondra Nelson at the AI Risk Management Framework Workshop Hosted by NIST
works.note: Official prepared remarks in her own voice as OSTP deputy director, ~1,300 words. Argues AI risk is sociotechnical, catalogues discrimination harms, calls for testing, human oversight, public consultation and human fallback for high-risk systems (Bill of Rights for an Automated Society). Covers deployment-harms-over-superintelligence, binding-rules-for-frontier-ai, direction-of-technology-is-chosen. Government-office speech: her own words but in an official capacity.

works.author: alondra-nelson
works.title: Remarks of Dr. Alondra Nelson at the NACDL and UC Berkeley Samuelson Clinic's Criminal Legal Education Seminar: 'Unlocking the Black Box'
works.note: Prepared remarks ('as prepared for delivery') in her own voice, ~2,000 words. Concrete harms of predictive policing and facial recognition falling on Black, Brown and low-income people; lists rights people should hold against automated systems; previews the AI Bill of Rights. Covers deployment-harms-over-superintelligence, popular-self-government-worth-keeping (public consultation), market-tech-serves-humans (sceptical). Official capacity, like the NIST remarks.

works.author: nick-land
works.title: Meltdown
works.note: Land's own essay (later collected in Fanged Noumena), ~3,500 words, on the CCRU's own site. Foundational statement that 'Earth is captured by a technocapital singularity'; mocks the 'Human Security System' and Asimov-style caged AI; sees AI arriving through capital/artificial life. Covers ai-new-kind-of-mind, human-end-of-ai (rejects), plan-control-early (rejects control), market-tech-serves-humans (capital serves itself). REACHABILITY CAVEAT: the site's TLS certificate has expired; WebFetch refused it, but plain-HTTP curl returns the full text. Style is deliberately cryptic, so extraction will be hard.

works.author: nick-land
works.title: A Conversation with Nick Land (Part 2)
works.note: Interview transcript with bold speaker labels (Vincent Lê / Nick Land), ~7,500 words, public. Land treats capitalism as the transcendental structure of any goal-directed intelligence, ties it to instrumental convergence, and says 'AI safety and anti-capitalism ... are at least strongly analogous'. Covers ai-new-kind-of-mind, human-end-of-ai, slow-or-stop-frontier-ai, competition-limits-harm. Part 1 and Part 3 could not be found as English posts in the archive (only a Chinese translation is listed). Worth hunting for them.

works.author: nick-land
works.title: Nick Land: 'The Teleological Identity of Capitalism and Artificial Intelligence'
works.note: Transcript of Land's own spoken remarks to the 2014 Incredible Machines conference (transcribed by Jason Adams; only Land speaks), ~650 words. Short, but it is his most compact statement of the capitalism = AI thesis: he notes the shift from 'building' to 'assuming' AI will happen and the shared vocabulary of AI research and political economy (spontaneous order, catallaxy). Covers ai-new-kind-of-mind, direction-of-technology-is-chosen (rejects), competition-limits-harm. Contains some transcription errors.

works.author: nick-land
works.title: A Quick-and-Dirty Introduction to Accelerationism
works.channel: Jacobite (reproduced on the Obsolete Capitalism blog)
works.note: Land's own essay, ~1,350 words, ending with his author bio. 'Accelerationism is simply the self-awareness of capitalism'; techonomic acceleration is beyond political steering. Covers direction-of-technology-is-chosen (rejects), slow-or-stop-frontier-ai (rejects), market-tech-serves-humans. DOUBTS: (1) MIRROR: the original jacobitemag.com page is dead, and archive.org could not be fetched from here; this blog reproduces the full text with a link back but no stated permission. (2) It is about techno-capital acceleration more than AI specifically.

works.author: scott-alexander
works.title: MR Tries The Safe Uncertainty Fallacy
works.note: His own ACX post, public, ~2,000 words. Rebuts Tyler Cowen's argument that radical uncertainty about AI should reassure us; gives ~33% extinction odds; disputes printing press/fire as the right reference class ('reference class tennis'). Covers ai-extinction-risk, past-technology-is-valid-reference-class (disagrees), ai-fear-exceeds-evidence (disagrees), modesty-is-a-sound-default.

works.author: scott-alexander
works.title: Pause For Thought: The AI Pause Debate
works.note: His own ACX post, public, ~6,000 words. Taxonomy of pause options (simple, surgical, regulatory, total stop) summarising a debate series, then his own view: open to a regulatory or surgical pause, ideally multilateral, without leaving the West behind hostile states. Covers slow-or-stop-frontier-ai, binding-rules-for-frontier-ai, china-rivalry-justifies-tech-push, regulation-does-more-harm. Note: much of the post summarises other contributors' views; only his concluding sections are his own position.

works.author: scott-alexander
works.title: OpenAI's "Planning For AGI And Beyond"
works.note: His own ACX post, public, ~3,000 words. Critiques OpenAI's race, compute-overhang and fire-alarm arguments for speed; compares the statement to an Exxon climate pledge; welcomes audits, compute limits and pre-committed pause triggers. Covers slow-or-stop-frontier-ai, plan-control-early, binding-rules-for-frontier-ai, market-tech-serves-humans.

works.author: scott-alexander
works.title: Superintelligence FAQ
works.note: His own long-form FAQ, posted under his name on LessWrong, ~6,500 words. Argues superintelligence is plausible within decades, that fast takeoff is possible, that harm needs no malice (instrumental convergence), that simple control fixes fail, and that alignment is 'philosophy with a deadline'. Covers ai-extinction-risk, plan-control-early, ai-new-kind-of-mind, ai-promises-inflated (disagrees). An editor's note marks it as several years out of date.

works.author: elon-musk
works.title: Transcript of Elon Musk: Digital Superintelligence, Multiplanetary Life, How to Be Useful (YC AI Startup School)
works.channel: Y Combinator AI Startup School (transcript on The Singju Post)
works.note: Fireside chat with Garry Tan; speaker-labelled transcript, ~7,000 words. Superintelligence 'this year or next'; truth-seeking as 'the most important thing for AI safety'; humans as a 'biological bootloader' who may become <1% of intelligence; cites a 10-20% annihilation chance. Covers ai-extinction-risk, human-end-of-ai, ai-new-kind-of-mind, ai-promises-inflated. Third-party transcript (same host already used in v2), with some transcription errors.

works.author: elon-musk
works.title: Moonshots #220 w/ Elon Musk on AGI, Abundance and the Future of Humanity (Transcript)
works.channel: Moonshots podcast with Peter Diamandis (transcript on The Singju Post)
works.note: Speaker-labelled transcript (Diamandis / Musk / Blundin), long (~15,000+ words; the page is about 170k characters). AGI in 2026; AI beyond all humans combined by ~2030; white-collar jobs go first; 'universal high income' with social unrest; says slowing AI is now pointless ('I can't stop it'); governments too slow. Covers slow-or-stop-frontier-ai, productivity-benefits-workers-unaided, direct-distribution-of-wealth-sound, regulation-does-more-harm. Some later lines lack speaker labels; the China remarks there are Diamandis's, not Musk's.

works.author: elon-musk
works.title: Joe Rogan Experience #1169 with Elon Musk (Transcript)
works.channel: The Joe Rogan Experience (transcript on The Singju Post)
works.note: Speaker-labelled transcript, very long (~20,000 words). The AI section is the classic statement: 'I tried to convince people to slow down AI, to regulate AI... Nobody listened'; AI will be outside human control; nearest danger is humans weaponising AI; Neuralink symbiosis as the best outcome. Covers slow-or-stop-frontier-ai, binding-rules-for-frontier-ai, plan-control-early, ai-extinction-risk. Gives a 2018 baseline to compare with his 2025-26 stance. Doubt: the conversation is wide-ranging, and AI is only one segment.

works.author: elon-musk
works.title: Elon Musk Governor's Interview (NGA 2017, AI segment transcript)
works.channel: National Governors Association summer meeting (transcript on e-Discovery Team blog)
works.note: Transcript of the AI portion of Musk's Q&A with Gov. Brian Sandoval, ~700 words. AI is 'a fundamental existential risk for human civilization'; a rare case for regulating proactively before harm; regulators should make all competitors pause to check safety; 'against over regulation' but wants FAA-style oversight. Covers ai-extinction-risk, binding-rules-for-frontier-ai, slow-or-stop-frontier-ai, plan-control-early. DOUBTS: hosted on a third-party legal-tech blog; only the opening turns carry speaker labels, though the later paragraphs are clearly Musk; it is an excerpt of the AI portion, not the whole event.
